prompt.context: Our client is a telecom Fortune 50 company. One of its divisions (landline) is facing high churn (3% per year). They have launched a direct mail campaign to try to re-attain some customers. They have kept all the information they had on their customers.
prompt.question: How can they make their direct mail strategy more effective?

clarifying_info.q: Why are customers switching to other providers?
clarifying_info.a: There is no significant difference in the quality of service provided — it is standard landline service. The client also provides other services such as broadband and wireless to meet diversified customer needs. Therefore, the main reason for customers to switch is price.

framework: 1. Better understand customers — identify the right customer segment to target
2. Ensure the content of the direct mail is effective
3. Ensure the channel used to deliver the campaign is effective

questions.prompt: What are the different ways to segment customers?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers: (1) Segment by customer type/needs — e.g., business vs. individual consumers; within business, large enterprise vs. small/medium. (2) Segment by lifetime economic value — revenue generated minus cost to serve, multiplied by tenure. Key insight: use profitability (not just revenue) because cost to serve varies by customer (frequency of service calls, late payments, etc.). The campaign should target customers with high lifetime economic value or high future economic potential.

questions.prompt: Given that price is the main churn driver, what should the content of the direct mail campaign focus on?
questions.guidance: The campaign content should directly address why customers left — price. Focus on current promotions and discounts to win back price-sensitive churned customers.

questions.prompt: How should the client decide which distribution channel to use for the campaign?
questions.guidance: Match channel cost to customer profitability: use higher-cost channels (e.g., standard US mail) for customers with higher profitability/lifetime value; use lower-cost channels (e.g., internet/email) for customers with lower profitability. This ensures ROI on the re-acquisition spend.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors drive the lifetime economic value of a customer?

categories.name: Revenue
ideas: Cross-sell/upsell revenue from broadband and wireless bundles

categories.name: Cost to Serve
ideas: Frequency of calls to service center

recommendation: Segment the churned customer base by lifetime profitability using existing data; prioritize re-acquisition efforts on high-value customers
Craft direct mail content around price promotions and discounts — the primary churn driver
Use premium channels (physical mail) for high-value segments and low-cost channels (email/digital) for lower-value segments to optimize campaign ROI
risks: Promotions may attract price-sensitive customers who churn again once the promotional period ends
Segmentation based on historical data may not reflect customers' current needs or financial situation
Competitors may respond with counter-offers, reducing the effectiveness of the campaign
next_steps: Analyze existing customer data to compute profitability scores for all churned customers
Design tiered promotional offers matched to profitability segments
Pilot the campaign with a small subset before full rollout to measure response rates and refine messaging
